items.question: Vad är hastighet och hur räknar man ut den?
items.short: Hastighet är hur lång sträcka något färdas per tidsenhet, och man räknar ut den genom att dela sträckan med tiden.
items.long: Hastighet är hur lång sträcka något färdas per tidsenhet, och man räknar ut den genom att dela sträckan med tiden. Med bokstäver skriver man att hastigheten v är lika med sträckan s delat med tiden t. Hastighet kan till exempel anges i meter per sekund eller i kilometer per timme, beroende på vilken enhet man använder för sträcka och tid. Om en bil kör hundra kilometer på två timmar är hastigheten femtio kilometer i timmen. Det är då en medelhastighet, eftersom bilen under resan kan ha kört både fortare och långsammare.

items.question: Hur räknar man om en meter per sekund till kilometer per timme?
items.short: En meter per sekund är samma sak som tre komma sex kilometer per timme, så man multiplicerar med tre komma sex.
items.long: En meter per sekund är samma sak som tre komma sex kilometer per timme, så man multiplicerar med tre komma sex. Vill man gå åt andra hållet, från kilometer per timme till meter per sekund, delar man i stället med tre komma sex. Tio meter per sekund blir alltså trettiosex kilometer per timme. Talet tre komma sex kommer av att en kilometer är tusen meter och en timme är tretusensexhundra sekunder.

Det kallas medelhastighet eftersom cyklisten säkert har cyklat fortare i nedförsbackar och långsammare i uppförsbackar, och tolv kilometer i timmen är det genomsnittliga värdet över hela turen.

items.question: Varför är det lätt att halka på is?
items.short: Friktionen mellan skon och isen är väldigt liten, så det finns nästan inget som bromsar skon från att glida.
items.long: Friktionen mellan skon och isen är väldigt liten, så det finns nästan inget som bromsar skon från att glida. Friktion är en kraft som bromsar rörelse mellan två ytor. På is är ytan så hal att kraften blir svag, och då räcker minsta sidorörelse för att foten ska glida iväg. På torr asfalt är friktionen stor, och därför står man stadigt där. Därför kan man halka även om man går försiktigt, och därför använder man broddar eller sand för att öka friktionen på isiga vägar.

items.question: Varför har däck mönster?
items.short: Mönstret ökar friktionen mellan däcket och vägen när det är blött, så bilen får bättre grepp.
items.long: Mönstret ökar friktionen mellan däcket och vägen när det är blött, så bilen får bättre grepp. Friktion är den kraft som bromsar rörelse mellan två ytor, och den behövs för att däcket ska greppa vägen vid acceleration, kurvtagning och inbromsning. När vägen är blöt kan ett slätt däck glida på vattenskiktet och friktionen blir liten, ungefär som på is. Mönstrets spår leder bort vatten så att gummit kommer i kontakt med vägen. Då håller bilen bättre och är lättare att styra och stanna.

items.question: Why is the Earth's climate getting warmer?
items.short: The Earth is getting warmer because humans burn coal, oil and gas, which releases carbon dioxide that traps more heat in the atmosphere.
items.long: The Earth is getting warmer because humans burn coal, oil and gas, which releases carbon dioxide that traps more heat in the atmosphere. This is called the greenhouse effect. Gases like carbon dioxide act like the glass roof of a greenhouse: sunlight gets in, but the heat cannot easily escape back into space. The more fossil fuels we burn, the more carbon dioxide there is, so more heat is trapped and the temperature keeps rising. Most scientists agree that people are the main cause of this change.

items.question: What does it mean that the average temperature has risen by 1.2 degrees since 1850?
items.short: It means that the Earth's average temperature today is about one point two degrees higher than it was around the year eighteen fifty.
items.long: It means that the Earth's average temperature today is about one point two degrees higher than it was around the year eighteen fifty. This may sound like a small change, but it is an average for the whole planet, so it affects a lot. Even a small rise in the average can melt ice on Greenland and Antarctica, which makes sea levels rise. It also makes heat waves, droughts and heavy rain more common around the world.

items.question: Who do most scientists believe is the main cause of global warming?
items.short: Most scientists agree that humans are the main cause of global warming.
items.long: Most scientists agree that humans are the main cause of global warming. The reason is that human activities, especially burning coal, oil and gas, release large amounts of carbon dioxide into the air. This gas traps heat in the atmosphere, so the more we release, the warmer the Earth becomes. Because people are the cause, people can also be part of the solution, for example by cutting emissions.

items.question: How does the greenhouse effect work?
items.short: Gases like carbon dioxide in the atmosphere trap heat from the sun, so the Earth stays warmer than it would be without them.
items.long: Gases like carbon dioxide in the atmosphere trap heat from the sun, so the Earth stays warmer than it would be without them. It works a bit like the glass roof of a greenhouse, which lets sunlight in but keeps the heat inside. When we burn coal, oil and gas, we release more carbon dioxide, so even more heat is trapped. This extra trapped heat is what makes the climate warmer. The effect becomes a problem when humans make it stronger than it naturally is.

items.question: Why are gases like carbon dioxide compared to the glass roof of a greenhouse?
items.short: They are compared to a glass roof because both trap heat: a glass roof keeps warmth inside a greenhouse, and carbon dioxide keeps heat in the atmosphere.
items.long: They are compared to a glass roof because both trap heat: a glass roof keeps warmth inside a greenhouse, and carbon dioxide keeps heat in the atmosphere. In a greenhouse, sunlight passes through the glass and warms the air inside, but the heat cannot easily get out again. In the same way, carbon dioxide in the atmosphere lets the sun's energy reach the Earth but holds on to the heat. With more carbon dioxide in the air, more heat is held in, and the planet becomes warmer. This comparison helps us understand why burning fossil fuels warms the Earth.

items.question: Why is more carbon dioxide released when we burn coal, oil and gas?
items.short: Coal, oil and gas contain a lot of carbon, and burning them makes that carbon combine with oxygen, so carbon dioxide is released into the air.
items.long: Coal, oil and gas contain a lot of carbon, and burning them makes that carbon combine with oxygen, so carbon dioxide is released into the air. These fuels are called fossil fuels because they were formed from plants and animals that lived millions of years ago, and the carbon in them has been stored underground ever since. When we burn them for electricity, heating or transport, that stored carbon goes into the atmosphere as carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that traps heat, so the more we burn, the more heat is trapped and the warmer the Earth becomes.

items.question: How does melting ice on Greenland and Antarctica cause problems for cities?
items.short: When the ice on Greenland and Antarctica melts, the water runs into the oceans and makes sea levels rise, which threatens cities close to the coast.
items.long: When the ice on Greenland and Antarctica melts, the water runs into the oceans and makes sea levels rise, which threatens cities close to the coast. The ice on these two huge areas of land holds a lot of water. As the Earth gets warmer, more of it melts, and the extra water ends up in the sea. Higher seas can flood streets and homes in coastal cities, and the problem gets worse with every year of warming. People may have to build walls to keep the water out or even move away from their homes.

items.question: Why are cities near the coast threatened when the sea level rises?
items.short: Cities near the coast lie close to the sea, so when the water level rises it can flood them and damage buildings, roads and homes.
items.long: Cities near the coast lie close to the sea, so when the water level rises it can flood them and damage buildings, roads and homes. The higher the sea gets, the further it can reach onto land, especially during storms and heavy rain, which are becoming more common. Many big cities are built by the coast, so millions of people could be affected. Flooding can destroy houses, harm important services and force people to leave. That is why rising seas are seen as one of the most serious results of global warming.

items.question: Why do polar bears lose their habitat?
items.short: Polar bears live on sea ice, and as the Earth gets warmer the ice melts, so they lose the place where they live and hunt.
items.long: Polar bears live on sea ice, and as the Earth gets warmer the ice melts, so they lose the place where they live and hunt. Global warming is caused mainly by humans burning fossil fuels, and the extra heat melts the ice in the Arctic. Polar bears need the ice to move around and to hunt, so when it disappears they have less food and less space. This shows how climate change does not only affect people but also animals, some of which may struggle to survive if the ice keeps shrinking.

items.question: What did countries promise in the Paris Agreement from 2015?
items.short: In the Paris Agreement from 2015, countries promised to reduce their emissions of greenhouse gases to slow down global warming.
items.long: In the Paris Agreement from 2015, countries promised to reduce their emissions of greenhouse gases to slow down global warming. The idea is that if all the countries cut their emissions, less heat will be trapped in the atmosphere and the temperature will not rise as fast. A promise like this needs countries to work together, because climate change is a problem for the whole world. People can help too, for example by taking the train instead of flying, eating less meat and wasting less food.

items.question: How can ordinary people help to reduce climate change?
items.short: Ordinary people can cut their own emissions, for example by taking the train instead of flying, eating less meat and wasting less food.
items.long: Ordinary people can cut their own emissions, for example by taking the train instead of flying, eating less meat and wasting less food. These choices matter because burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, and carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere. Every flight we skip means less fuel burned and less carbon dioxide released. Many people making the same small choices can add up to a real difference. Countries have also promised to lower their emissions in the Paris Agreement, so what people do at home works together with what governments do.

items.question: What can people do in daily life to help the climate, according to what you have learned?
items.short: People can take the train instead of flying, eat less meat and waste less food, because all of these help to reduce emissions.
items.long: People can take the train instead of flying, eat less meat and waste less food, because all of these help to reduce emissions. Flying burns a lot of fuel, so travelling by train is a good choice. Choosing less meat and throwing away less food are also ways people can help, and together such choices support what countries promised in the Paris Agreement.

items.question: Hur såg skattefördelningen ut mellan de tre stånden i Frankrike före revolutionen?
items.short: Tredje ståndet var nästan hela befolkningen men betalade nästan alla skatter, medan prästerna och adeln, som hade mest rikedom och makt, betalade mycket lite.

Det gjorde samhället orättvist, eftersom bönder, hantverkare och borgare bar nästan hela bördan utan att få något inflytande över hur pengarna användes. Skatterna blev särskilt tunga när staten var nära konkurs och kungen behövde mer pengar. Missnöjet i tredje ståndet var en av de viktigaste orsakerna till att revolutionen bröt ut.

items.question: Vad innebar ståndssamhället i Frankrike före revolutionen?
items.short: Ståndssamhället delade in befolkningen i tre grupper: prästerna, adeln och alla andra, och vilken grupp man föddes in i avgjorde ens rättigheter och skyldigheter.

Tredje ståndet var nästan hela befolkningen men betalade nästan alla skatter. Samhället byggde alltså på ojämlikhet, och det skapade ett stort missnöje som bidrog till att revolutionen bröt ut år sjuttonhundraåttionio.

items.question: Varför var den franska staten nära konkurs före revolutionen?
items.short: Staten var nära konkurs eftersom Frankrike hade fört dyra krig, bland annat genom stödet till den amerikanska revolutionen, och därför gick statens utgifter långt över dess inkomster.

items.question: What does the theme of courage mean in the story?

items.question: What does the word keeper mean, and how is it used in the story?

items.question: What does the expression in spite of mean?
items.short: In spite of means despite something, that is, something happens even though another thing is present or tries to stop it.
